societies.name: Mizora — The technological women’s commonwealth
societies.society: The admitted female resident population supported by automata and chemical production

scope.period: The established society visited by Vera before her return home
scope.population: Living admitted Mizoran women and daughters
exclusions: Men or excluded racial groups as equal beneficiaries
Historical elimination as a measured present population
The critic’s speculative exact punishment methods as canon

societies.description:
Mizora combines automata performing domestic work, advanced chemical food production and an order described as free from poverty. This provides a real technological reduction of necessary labor within the admitted resident population. Guarantees are provisionally favorable for those residents, with a wide interval because universal prosperity is presented through a highly exclusionary vision. The novel’s eugenics, racial hierarchy and removal of men remain explicit boundaries, not erased by the word utopia.

The surviving women direct the technology, but the short references do not establish how equally productive assets or ultimate decisions are controlled. Control therefore remains unresolved rather than equating a commonwealth label with distributed ownership or inventing an AI ruler. The state’s coercive control of bodies and belonging is distinct from routine machine operation. Chemical food and domestic automation also do not remove scholarship, care, art or other useful human activities. No all-person participation census is available, so nonworking remains null. The point concerns the functioning resident order and does not turn excluded or eliminated people into nonworkers receiving its benefits.

guarantees.basis: The references specifically combine domestic automata, chemically produced food and absence of poverty for the admitted resident population, with severe exclusion.

societies.name: News from Nowhere — The chosen handicraft commonwealth
societies.society: Commonly owned production retaining pleasurable human labor despite machine capacity

scope.population: Living human residents of the commonwealth
exclusions: Machine rejection as lack of technical capacity
The retained labor as a modern paid-job protection program

societies.description:
The commonwealth deliberately returns to handicraft after machines have become capable of performing almost all necessary work. Chapter XXVII says this directly: retained handwork is a preference rather than material necessity. This makes the society a particularly clear zero variant. Its reason is the pursuit of pleasurable, creative labor and equality, not an attempt to preserve conventional wage employment. Useful making remains part of ordinary life.

Common ownership and democratic control of productive resources place control toward the distributed human end. Goods are not allocated through private money or a class hierarchy, supporting strong guarantees within the shared order, though the references do not provide a comprehensive enforceable necessities charter. Voluntary and enjoyable work still counts as work, so the disappearance of wages cannot provide a nonworking percentage. The record covers the established handicraft period; earlier machine-intensive transition phases are not counted again without a separate economic assessment. Its zero label describes a realized choice among productive possibilities rather than technological backwardness.

societies.name: The Republic of the Future — New York Socialist City
societies.society: Mechanized collective domestic provision in Dodd’s satirical future

scope.continuity: Anna Bowman Dodd’s original epistolary novella
scope.period: The New York Socialist City visited in 2050
scope.population: Living human inhabitants of Socialist City
exclusions: Two-hour days as proof everyone is nonworking
Authorial disdain as independent evidence that material provision fails

societies.description:
Socialist City provides a standardized technological living environment in which manufactured nutrition is delivered to homes through tubes and automatic devices handle domestic tasks. Residents still work short days, but centralized mechanization supplies much of ordinary life and sharply reduces necessary household labor. Guarantees receive a qualified favorable estimate for that collective provision; plainness and lack of variety are not the same as absence of food or housing.

Effective control is near concentrated human public authority. Uniform consumption and nominal socialism do not establish each resident’s equal ability to govern the productive system, while automatic lifts and bedmaking devices are not sovereign AI. The narrator and author treat this future satirically, so their dislike is distinguished from the depicted technical arrangement. Real work remains, including the reported two-hour daily contribution. Hours worked are not the share of people who work at all, and useful care or creative activity cannot be ignored. Nonworking therefore stays unresolved rather than being calculated from a shortened workday.

review_notes: Twelve sequential reference checks yield three records, including a directly evidenced News from Nowhere zero variant.
Mizora guarantees are scoped to admitted women/daughters; racial and eugenic exclusions are not hidden and no speculative punishment method is asserted.
News from Nowhere Chapter XXVII explicitly establishes capacity for almost all necessary work and chosen handicraft. Enjoyable work remains useful.
Dodd’s short workday is not a participation fraction. Manufactured food and domestic automation are actual mechanisms, while narrative satire is separated from provision.
No complete old novel, magazine, primary PDF or elaborate format reconstruction was used to rescue weak leads.
Real Mizoram enterprises, historical radio/music broadcasts and unrelated technical papers were discarded.
